correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=2 and real 0<=x<=1, the affine image of a uniform simplex conditional on k specified gaps exceeding x is uniform on a smaller simplex. Its first two Dirichlet moments, inclusion–exclusion, and three beta integrals rigorously give the stated exact weighted-tail law and harmonic covariance. The harmonic recurrence proves strict positivity; Dirichlet fourth moments and maximal-spacing second moment prove the precise correlation and its decay. Exact rational checks at n=2..39 and independent 2- and 3-dimensional integrals corroborate finite instances, not the infinite proof.

Primary sources inspected give the maximum-gap marginal and Greenwood statistic separately, not the joint weighted-tail polynomial; searches also found no direct match. value.rationale: The longest gap and Greenwood quadratic spacing statistic are separate natural uniformity diagnostics. Their marginals alone provide no adjustment for joint selection. The exact threshold-dependent conditional Greenwood mean quantifies selection induced by screening for large gaps at every sample size; its positive covariance and sharp vanishing standardized correlation resolve distinct finite/infinite notions of dependence. This is an exact natural cross-statistic not an arbitrary numerological slice.
